ads_ratio.reason: Philips trades in New York as New York Registry Shares: one NYSE-traded PHG share is one common (ordinary) share, so EDGAR per-share figures and the traded price are already on the same basis and no ADS scaling applies.
ads_ratio.source: Philips Form 20-F, Exhibit 2 (Description of Securities Registered under Section 12 of the Exchange Act, SEC filing, CIK 313216): the class registered under Section 12(b) and trading on the NYSE under PHG is 'Common Shares - par value Euro (EUR) 0.20 per share'; holders of New York Registry shares hold the common shares themselves in registered form — the NYSE security is the common share, not an ADS

moat_against: GE HealthCare and Siemens Healthineers match Philips category by category; no durable technology gap
Respironics recall fallout: FDA consent decree restricts US sleep/respiratory device sales, DOJ investigation still open, ~$1.1B personal-injury settlement paid in 2025
Hospital capital budgets are cyclical and price-competitive; China health-system demand is weak
A decade of roughly flat comparable sales (2026 guide only 3-4.5%) shows weak pricing power
Net debt 5.0x normalized owner's earnings leaves little room for another recall-scale shock
moat_for: Top-3 global franchise in diagnostic imaging, image-guided therapy (Azurion) and hospital patient monitoring, with a large installed base
Installed base drives recurring service, parts and software revenue and real switching costs for hospital platforms
Regulatory clearances and clinical validation are genuine entry barriers in imaging and monitoring
Scale R&D and AI imaging pipeline (e.g. SmartIQ for Azurion) plus a record equipment order backlog
moat_justification: Moderate, narrow moat: a top-3 global position in diagnostic imaging, image-guided therapy and hospital patient monitoring with a large installed base, multi-year service contracts and regulatory-clearance barriers — but GE HealthCare and Siemens Healthineers contest every category, hospital capex is cyclical and price-competitive, the Respironics consent decree bars Philips from the US sleep-therapy device market until FDA conditions are met, and a decade of flat comparable growth shows limited pricing power.
name: Koninklijke Philips N.V. (Royal Philips)
one_liner: Solid health-tech franchise, moat 5/10, but owner's earnings are still depressed by Respironics settlement outflows and net debt is 5.0x normalized OE — at $25.18 it does not clear 15% (weighted IRR 7.85%, weighted IV@15 $10.70); clears 15% only below ~$10.70.
